verdict.label: BEARISH — Weekend Capitulation: BTC Tags ~$59K, ~$390B Erased, Strategy Turns Seller
verdict.rationale_short: The Friday break became a weekend capitulation. BTC tagged a low near ~$59,227 and ETH broke below $1,900, extending crypto's weekly decline past 11% as roughly $390B in market value was erased and ~$7B in leveraged positions were liquidated. The selling is now structural, not just macro: Strategy (MicroStrategy) disclosed its first bitcoin sale, spot-BTC-ETF outflows exceeded $3.2B, and a Mt. Gox wallet transfer added supply overhang. With equities closed and the US and Iran trading strikes near Hormuz, there is no stabilizing bid this weekend. BEARISH at medium conviction — actively de-risked, not bottom-fishing — until forced selling exhausts and the macro (CPI June 10) clears.

supporting_data.label: BTC bottomed near ~$59,227 over the weekend before steadying; ETH broke below $1,900, lifting the weekly decline past 11%; roughly $390B in crypto value erased and ~$7B in leveraged positions liquidated

Structural supply shock: Strategy (MicroStrategy) disclosed its first bitcoin sale — the largest corporate holder turning seller — alongside >$3.2B in spot-BTC-ETF outflows and a Mt. Gox wallet transfer

Macro backdrop hostile and worsening: equities broke Friday (SPX -2.64%, VIX ~20.9, 30Y above 5.0%), and over the weekend the US and Iran exchanged strikes near the Strait of Hormuz, straining the ceasefire
Total crypto market cap is now down roughly 48% from its 2026 peak — a drawdown with no valuation floor to defend, set by supply, demand, and narrative alone

watchlist_mentions.note: Tagged ~$59,227 — capitulation territory, but with Strategy selling and ETF outflows the bid is structurally weaker. A close below $59K opens $52-55K. No long.
Broke below $1,900 (~$1,710), -11% on the week; $1,674 is the line that must reclaim before any recovery; below it, $1,500.
Disclosed its first bitcoin sale — the most important single development: the largest corporate buyer is now a seller, removing a structural bid.
Down hard in the liquidation cascade; alts always worse in capitulation. Avoid until BTC bases.

dont_buy.reason: Forced selling (Strategy, ETF outflows, liquidations) plus a weekend Iran escalation means the supply overhang is not done; capitulation lows are often re-tested
dont_buy.better_entry: Wait for forced selling to exhaust and CPI June 10; require a reclaim of $66K BTC / $1,674 ETH

dont_buy.reason: Liquidation cascades hit alts hardest; ~$7B already wiped
dont_buy.better_entry: Only after BTC stabilizes and dominance peaks

trade_setups.thesis: A structural supply shock (Strategy selling, $3.2B ETF outflows, Mt. Gox) on top of a macro break and a weekend Iran escalation is a capitulation to respect from the sidelines, not to buy into. Preserve capital until forced selling clears.
trade_setups.entry: Hold cash/stables; no new risk this weekend
trade_setups.invalidation: Forced-selling exhaustion + BTC reclaim of $66,000 on a cool CPI

trade_setups.thesis: Below the $59K capitulation low, the next air pocket is $52-55K. With the largest corporate holder selling and ETF outflows accelerating, the path of least resistance stays down until the macro turns. Manage tightly given how stretched the move already is.
trade_setups.entry: Tactical short/hedge only on a daily close below $59,000; cover into $54-55K
trade_setups.invalidation: Reclaim of $62,000 on rising volume — cover; capitulation may be in

bear_case: This is the rare moment when the bear case is the base case: a ~48%-from-peak market with no valuation floor is now facing forced selling from its single largest corporate holder, accelerating ETF outflows, and a Mt. Gox overhang, all while the macro that caused the break (higher-for-longer rates, an Iran conflict feeding inflation) is unresolved and escalating. Capitulation lows tend to be re-tested before they hold. Invalidation: a reclaim of $62,000 on rising volume suggests the low is in; a daily close below $59,000 confirms the next leg toward $52-55K.
